## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Ambāṭakadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 439) is a verse narrative preserved in the Therāpadāna of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Belonging to the biographical apadāna genre, its title denotes the account of an elder (*thera*) who achieved spiritual distinction through the gift of hog-plum fruit (*ambāṭaka*). SuttaCentral indexes five translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].
No curated parallels in other Buddhist traditions are recorded on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. However, DharmaNexus identifies 101 machine-detected textual reuse matches shared across 47 other Pali texts, reflecting the highly formulaic structure of apadāna verse compositions [DharmaNexus]. Its largest Pali-internal overlap is with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (Paṭhamo bhāgo), matching seven passages (notably §1.4–3.1) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, extensive stretches of verse (especially within segments §2.1–7.1) are shared with numerous other fruit-donation apadānas, including the *Ajeliphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 509), *Labujadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 384), *Bhallātadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 446), and *Amodaphaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 510) [DharmaNexus]. A minor automatic cross-language match with a Tibetan Kangyur text (BO_K10_D0343_H0351) is detected with a very low plausibility score and remains unverified as a historical parallel [DharmaNexus].
